\[ f(14, 52) = \frac{52}{66} f(14, 66). \]

\[ f(14, 66) = \frac{33}{26} f(14, 52). \]

Plugging this back into our first equation:
\[ 66 \cdot \frac{33}{26} f(14, 52) = 52 f(14, 66). \]
\[ \frac{2178}{26} f(14, 52) = 52 f(14, 66). \]

We continue this process until we directly access \( f(14, 52) \) in the first property. Let's denote \( f(14, 52) = x \):
\[ f(14, 66) = \frac{1089}{52} x. \]
\[ f(14, 70) = \frac{1089}{52} \cdot \frac{1089}{52} x = \left( \frac{1089}{52} \right)^2 x. \]

From this pattern, we can see that for any \( n \):
\[ f(14, n) = \left( \frac{1089}{52} \right)^{\frac{n-14}{52}} x. \]

Thus, substituting \( n = 52 \):
\[ f(14, 52) = \left( \frac{1089}{52} \right)^\frac{46}{52} x. \]
\[ f(14, 52) = \left( \frac{1089}{52} \right)^\frac{23}{26} x. \]

Next, we need to simplify \(\frac{1089}{52} \):
\[ 1089 = 3^2 \cdot 11^2. \]

So we can write:
\[ \frac{1089}{52} = \frac{3^2 \cdot 11^2}{2^2 \cdot 13} = \frac{3^2 \cdot 11^2}{2^2 \cdot 13}. \]

The fourth power of this expression is:
\[ \left( \frac{1089}{52} \right)^{23} = 3^{46} \cdot 11^{46}. \]

Thus:
\[ f(14, 52) = 3^{46} \cdot 11^{46} x. \]
